title: Foresight
connection: Advent opens with the command to watch. Foresight is the virtue of looking ahead, reading the signs, and anticipating what God is bringing.

title: Preparedness
liturgicalContext: Advent 2 — John the Baptist: "Prepare the way"
connection: The Baptist's entire mission is preparation. Preparedness (caution) means taking practical steps now for what lies ahead.

title: Prayer
connection: Gaudete Sunday calls us to rejoice — and the means is prayer. Paul's command in 1 Thessalonians 5:17 makes prayer the virtue of this joyful week.

title: Humility
connection: Mary's fiat — "Let it be done to me" — is the supreme act of humility. She receives the greatest mission in history without a trace of self-assertion.

title: Adoration
connection: Shepherds fall to their knees. Angels sing. The only fitting response to the Incarnation is adoration — giving God the worship that is His due.

title: Generosity
liturgicalContext: Epiphany / Baptism of the Lord — The Magi bring gifts
connection: The Magi travel far and offer their finest treasures. Epiphany reveals that the generous heart recognizes the King.

title: Teachability
liturgicalContext: OT Week 2 — "Come and see" / Calling of disciples
connection: The first disciples drop everything to learn from Jesus. Teachability is the willingness to be formed by a master — the starting point of discipleship.

title: Courage
connection: Leaving nets, tax booths, and families requires fortitude. The call to follow Christ is always a call to be brave.

title: Truthfulness
connection: The Beatitudes turn the world's values upside down. Only the truthful person can receive these hard sayings without flinching.

title: Integrity
liturgicalContext: OT Week 5 — "You are salt and light"
connection: Salt that loses its flavor is thrown out. Light hidden under a basket serves no one. Integrity means being the same person inside and out — radiant and uncompromised.

title: Reasoning
liturgicalContext: OT Week 6 — "You have heard it said… but I say to you"
connection: Jesus deepens the Mosaic Law through rigorous moral reasoning. He does not abolish but fulfills — showing that reason illuminated by faith goes deeper than the letter.

title: Forgiveness
connection: The most radical command in the Gospel. Forgiveness is the temperance virtue that restrains our instinct for retaliation and frees us to love beyond merit.

title: Practical Wisdom
liturgicalContext: OT Week 8 — "The wise man built on rock"
connection: The capstone of the Sermon on the Mount. Prudence — practical wisdom — is the master virtue that builds one's life on the solid foundation of Christ's teaching.

title: Restraint
liturgicalContext: Lent 1 — Ash Wednesday / Temptation in the Desert
connection: Lent begins with fasting. Jesus refuses bread, spectacle, and power. Restraint — the habit of saying no to legitimate goods for a higher purpose — is the gateway to Lenten conversion.

title: Fasting
connection: The disciples glimpse glory on Tabor but must descend. Fasting strips away comfort so that we can see clearly — the Transfiguration reveals what fasting prepares us to behold.

title: Self-Discipline
connection: Mid-Lent deepens the call to interior conversion. Self-discipline is the cardinal virtue itself — the ordering of desires so that what we want serves what we love.

title: Gentlefirmness
connection: The father runs to meet his wayward son — gentle in embrace yet firm in truth. Meekness is not weakness but strength held in check by love. Laetare's joy springs from this tender reunion.

title: Perseverance
liturgicalContext: Lent 5 — "Unless a grain of wheat falls and dies…"
connection: Jesus sets his face toward Jerusalem. The grain must fall. Perseverance is the fortitude to keep going when the cost becomes clear and the road narrows.

title: Sacrifice
liturgicalContext: Holy Week / Palm Sunday — The Passion
connection: Christ lays down His life — the just offering that restores what sin has broken. Sacrifice is the justice virtue of giving to God what is most costly because He is most worthy.

title: Gratitude
connection: Alleluia! Death is conquered. Gratitude is the only adequate response — not earning, not striving, but receiving the gift of life with overflowing thanks.

title: Big-Souledness
liturgicalContext: Easter 2 (Divine Mercy Sunday) — Thomas touches the wounds
connection: Thomas moves from doubt to "My Lord and my God!" — the most expansive act of faith in the Gospels. Magnanimity, big-souledness, is the courage to believe greatly.

title: Understanding
connection: "Were not our hearts burning?" The Emmaus disciples' eyes are opened through Scripture. Understanding — the prudence virtue that grasps the meaning beneath the surface — turns grief into recognition.

title: Devotion
liturgicalContext: Easter 4 (Good Shepherd Sunday) — "I am the Good Shepherd"
connection: The shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. Devotion is the prompt willingness to give oneself entirely to God's service — the shepherd's defining quality.

title: Commitment
liturgicalContext: Easter 5 — "I am the vine, you are the branches"
connection: "Abide in me." To remain on the vine is a choice renewed daily. Commitment is the justice virtue of following through on what we have promised — staying grafted to Christ.

title: Friendliness
liturgicalContext: Easter 6 — "I call you friends" / The New Commandment
connection: "I no longer call you servants but friends." The risen Christ elevates His disciples into friendship. Friendliness is the virtue that makes us approachable, warm, and present to others.

title: Diligence
liturgicalContext: Ascension / Easter 7 — "Go and make disciples of all nations"
connection: The Great Commission demands industrious effort. Diligence — the measured, sustained application of energy to the work at hand — is how the Church carries out the Ascension mandate.

title: Creativity
liturgicalContext: Pentecost — The Holy Spirit descends in fire and wind
connection: The Spirit speaks in every tongue, invents new ways to reach every heart. Creativity — the prudence virtue of finding unexpected solutions — is the Spirit's signature gift.

title: Memory
connection: The Church recalls the deepest mystery of God's inner life. Memory — the prudence virtue of holding truth present in the mind — is how we treasure what has been revealed.

title: Generous Giving
liturgicalContext: Corpus Christi — "This is my Body, given for you"
connection: God holds nothing back. In the Eucharist, He gives His entire self. Generous giving — the habit of offering our substance, not just our surplus — mirrors this total gift.

title: Worship
connection: The Solemnity of the Sacred Heart invites us into the burning love of Christ's own heart. Worship — the virtue of rendering God the honor due to Him — is our entry into that fire.

title: Justice
connection: Peter the rock. Paul the apostle to the nations. Together they establish the Church's order in truth and right relationship. Justice itself — giving each person what is due — is their shared legacy.

title: Sound Judgment
connection: Thomas demanded evidence. Jesus honored the demand. Sound judgment — the capacity to assess a situation rightly — leads Thomas from skepticism to the greatest confession of faith.

title: Obedience
connection: "Listen" — the first word of St. Benedict's Rule. Benedictine obedience is not servile compliance but the deep listening that orients the whole person toward God's will.

title: Respect
connection: "Rabboni!" — Mary Magdalene greets the risen Lord with reverent awe. Respect (observance) is the justice virtue of honoring those who are set above us, beginning with Christ Himself.

title: Filial Piety
connection: The grandparents of Jesus. Filial piety — the love and honor owed to parents and ancestors — is embodied in the hidden faithfulness of Joachim and Anne, who prepared the way for Mary.

title: Good Counsel
liturgicalContext: OT Week 18 — Summer parables of the kingdom
connection: The kingdom parables (treasure in a field, pearl of great price) invite deliberation: what is worth everything? Good counsel is the virtue of seeking and giving wise advice before acting.

title: Alertness
connection: "This is my beloved Son — listen to Him!" Alertness — attentiveness to all the circumstances around us — is what the drowsy disciples on Tabor most needed, and what Dominic exercised in founding the Order of Preachers.

title: Poise
connection: Mary is taken up body and soul into heaven — the ultimate composure before God. Poise is the temperance virtue of carrying oneself with dignity and grace, neither anxious nor presumptuous.

title: Self-Control
connection: "Grant me chastity and continence — but not yet." Augustine's long struggle and eventual victory make him the patron of self-control: the power to master disordered desires through grace.

title: Gracefulness
liturgicalContext: Birth of the Blessed Virgin Mary (September 8)
connection: Mary enters the world with quiet grace. Gracefulness — beauty in movement and manner — reflects the inner order of one who is "full of grace."

title: Patience
connection: The Cross is not just endured but exalted. Patience is the fortitude to bear suffering without being broken — transforming pain into offering.

title: Sobriety
connection: Mary stands at the foot of the Cross with clear-eyed grief — no hysteria, no denial. Sobriety is the temperance of a mind that remains unclouded even in the deepest pain.

title: Strategic Wisdom
connection: Michael battles the dragon. Gabriel delivers the message. Raphael guides the journey. Strategic wisdom — the capacity to coordinate complex efforts toward victory — is the archangels' gift.

title: Orderliness
connection: The "Little Way" — doing small things with great love, in order. St. Thérèse found holiness not in grand gestures but in the careful ordering of daily life toward God.

title: Playing Well
liturgicalContext: St. Francis of Assisi (Oct 4) / Our Lady of the Rosary (Oct 7)
connection: Francis preached to birds, danced with Brother Sun, and called death "Sister." Playing well — the virtue of wholesome recreation and joy — is the Franciscan charism: finding delight in God's creation.

title: Personal Wisdom
connection: Teresa mapped the soul's journey through seven mansions. Personal wisdom — prudence directed at one's own spiritual growth — is the interior knowledge she cultivated and taught.

title: Equity
connection: Luke, the physician-evangelist, tells the stories of the poor, the outcast, the Samaritan. Equity — the virtue of applying the spirit of the law when the letter falls short — pervades his Gospel.

title: Fair Exchange
connection: The "hidden apostles" gave their lives for the Gospel and received the crown. Fair exchange — the justice of equal giving and receiving — is fulfilled in martyrdom: life given, eternal life received.

title: Modesty
connection: The saints include kings and beggars, doctors and peasants — but all are clothed in white. Modesty, the virtue of presenting oneself appropriately, reminds us that holiness is the only garment that matters.

title: Chasteness
liturgicalContext: All Souls / OT Week 32 — Parable of the wise and foolish virgins
connection: The wise virgins kept their lamps burning. Chasteness — purity of heart and body — is the oil that keeps the flame alive as we await the Bridegroom.

title: Just Correction
liturgicalContext: OT Week 33 — Parable of the talents / End-time accountability
connection: The master returns and settles accounts. Just correction — the virtue of righting wrongs and holding others accountable with fairness — is the theme of these eschatological parables.

title: Fair Distribution
liturgicalContext: Christ the King — "Whatever you did for the least of these…"
connection: The final Sunday of the liturgical year. Christ the King judges the nations: did you feed the hungry, clothe the naked, visit the prisoner? Fair distribution — giving to each according to their need — is the measure of His kingdom.
